title: ISE ERS / OpenAPI Brute-Force, Token Theft, and Anomalous API-Caller Detection
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'ISE ERS / OpenAPI Brute-Force, Token Theft, and Anomalous API-Caller Detection' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_ise_ers_openapi_brute_force_token_theft_and_anom` (UC-17.1.57), SOC dashboard panel "Network — ISE ERS / OpenAPI Brute-Force, Token Theft, and Anomalous API-Caller Detection", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.assurance_rationale: Art.21(2)(b) — incident handling on API access abuse.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=nac` sourcetype='cisco:ise:syslog' that satisfy the UC-17.1.57 SPL filters for 'ISE ERS / OpenAPI Brute-Force, Token Theft, and Anomalous API-Caller Detection'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `nac` / `cisco:ise:syslog` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.57.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *Administrative and Operational Audit* category — codes `52001` (ERS / OpenAPI auth success), `52002` (ERS / OpenAPI auth failure), `52003` (ERS / OpenAPI authz denied), `52004` (ERS / OpenAPI rate-limit). Fields: `api_user`, `client_ip`, `endpoint_path`, `http_method`, `http_status`. CIM mapping: `Authentication.action`.
spl:
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (52002, 52003, 52004)
| stats count, dc(client_ip) as unique_ips, dc(endpoint_path) as unique_paths by api_user
| where count > 50 OR (unique_ips > 5 AND count > 20)
description: Detects ERS / OpenAPI brute-force attempts, token theft (one user from many IPs), and anomalous high-volume callers — symptoms of compromised API credentials or misuse.
value: ISE's ERS/OpenAPI exposes the entire control plane. A compromised API token can be used to read endpoint inventory, modify auth policies, or push ANC actions. Detecting brute-force or anomalous use within 5 minutes is the primary defense.
implementation: Confirm *Administrative and Operational Audit* at INFO. Schedule every 5 min, search window `-15m@m to @m`, throttle on `api_user` for 30 min.
visualization: (1) Single value: API-failure events last 1h. (2) Top-N: API users by failure count. (3) Map: client_ip distribution.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'ISE ERS / OpenAPI Brute-Force, Token Theft, and Anomalous API-Caller Detection'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=nac` `cisco:ise:syslog` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• ISE ERS / OpenAPI enabled.
• `api_users.csv` with `api_user`, `expected_caller_ip`, `expected_endpoint_paths`.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable *Administrative and Operational Audit* at INFO.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field.

A secondary anomaly check matches `client_ip` against `api_users.csv` `expected_caller_ip`:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode=52001 earliest=-1h
| lookup api_users.csv api_user OUTPUT expected_caller_ip
| where !match(client_ip, expected_caller_ip)
```

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — API Access Audit":
• Single value: failures last 1h.
• Top-N users.
• Map of caller IPs.

Alerting: PagerDuty high on brute-force; medium on caller-IP anomaly.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **Bursts of 52004 (rate-limit)** — Tune ISE rate-limit OR fix the offending integration's polling cadence.
• **52002 from internal dev IP** — Dev iterating on a script; coordinate.
• **Persistent 52003 (authz denied)** — User has wrong role; review.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`api_user, unique_ips`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: ISE has an interface for other systems to connect to it. We watch for too many wrong passwords or unusual patterns of use — these can mean someone is trying to break in or has stolen a password.
